Hi Jeff —

Thanks for the request. I'm Rachel Kim (Director of Security) at Redwood; below is a concise summary we use to answer SIG/CAIQ/SOC 2 VM questions. I attached a short PDF overview and the SIG-formatted response document for BrightFinance to ingest into your questionnaire. If you need additional exported artifacts (raw scanner CSVs, signed attestation), we can provide redacted exports over secure share.

Scan cadence (production):
- Continuous vulnerability metadata updates via our agentized pipeline; automated critical-issue alerts are generated in near real-time.
- Weekly authenticated host/container scans for production pools (scheduled rolling windows to avoid disruption).
- Monthly full-environment authenticated scans that include all services and long‑running instances.
- Weekly critical-only quick scans (targeted) run daily for high-exposure tiers when risk indicators spike.
- Quarterly third‑party penetration testing (external vendor) and annual architecture review.

Tooling and coverage: Tenable.io for host/container vuln scanning, Prisma Cloud for IaC and container runtime checks, and tracer-validated SBOMs for dependency vuln mapping. We correlate findings into our ticketing system (Jira) and into the Redwood Console for traceability.

Remediation SLA (typical windows from detection to verified closure):
- Critical (actively exploitable remote code execution, high-impact): 72 hours (target 24–48 hours where practicable)
- High (privilege escalation, data exposure risk): 14 calendar days
- Medium (moderate impact/config issue): 30 calendar days
- Low (informational/low-risk): 90 calendar days

Exception and acceptance process:
- Exceptions are formally requested in Jira (project: SEC-EXC) with a compensating-controls plan and a documented rollback/mitigation strategy.
- Exception requests require Security reviewer + Service Owner approval; high-impact exceptions escalate to Security Council and may require Exec sign-off.
- Temporary exceptions are time-boxed (default max 90 days) and include mandatory compensating controls such as network segmentation, enhanced logging/retention, and increased scanning frequency.
- We track exceptions in an auditable CSV export and attach the redacted ticket for external review.

Attestation statement (short):
I attest that the vulnerability management cadence and SLA windows described are in effect for production services run by Redwood Inference and that exceptions are managed through our documented SEC-EXC Jira flow.

— Rachel Kim
Director, Information Security
Redwood Inference

Drive folder (redacted evidence + templates): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_example_drive_link

If you confirm which artifacts you need (redacted ticket, exception log, signed SOC‑2 attestation), we'll package and send them over an encrypted share. Happy to schedule a 30-min call next week to walk through the packet.
